questions.problem:
Given that $f(x)=\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4x-5},$ which of the following statements is correct?

I. ${lim}_{x\to (-5)^{+}}f(x)=+\infty $

II. ${lim}_{x\to (-5)^{-}}f(x)=+\infty $

III. ${lim}_{x\to (-5)}f(x)=-\infty $
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4x-5} \\  & =\frac{x}{(x-1)(x+5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

The function $f(x)=\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4x-5}$ has two vertical asymptotes $x=1$ and $x=-5.$

To compute the one-sided limits as $x\to (-5),$ we evaluate $f(x)$ at $x$-values very close to $x=-5$ from the right and from the left.

| $x$ | $-5.1$ | $-5.01$ | $-5$ | $-4.99$ | $-4.9$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $-8.36$ | $-83.36$ | $\text{undefined}$ | $83.30$ | $8.30$ |

All values are negative and get smaller and smaller as $x\to (-5)$ from the left and all values are positive and get larger and larger as $x\to (-5)$ from the right. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-5)^{-}}f(x)=-\infty ,\,\,\,{lim}_{x\to (-5)^{+}}f(x)=+\infty .
$$

Consequently, statement I is true and II is false.

Finally, since both left and right-sided limits at $x=-5$ are different, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-5)}f(x)=\text{DNE},
$$

and therefore III is false.

In conclusion, only statement I is true. A plot of the function is shown below.

questions.problem:
Given that $f(x)=\frac{x}{6+x-{x}^{2}},$ which of the following statements is correct?

I. ${lim}_{x\to (-2)^{-}}f(x)=-\infty $

II. ${lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}f(x)=-\infty $

III. ${lim}_{x\to (-2)}f(x)=\text{DNE}$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x}{6+x-{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{x}{(x-3)(x+2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

This implies that the function $f(x)=\frac{x}{6+x-{x}^{2}}$ has two vertical asymptotes $x=-2$ and $x=3.$

To compute the one-sided limits as $x\to (-2),$ we evaluate $f(x)$ at $x$-values very close to $x=-2$ from the right and from the left.

| $x$ | $-2.01$ | $-2.001$ | $-2$ | $-1.999$ | $-1.99$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $≈40.12$ | $≈400.12$ | $\text{undefined}$ | $≈-399.88$ | $≈-39.88$ |

All values are positive and get larger and larger as $x\to (-2)$ from the left and all values are negative and get smaller and smaller as $x\to (-2)$ from the right. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{-}}f(x)=+\infty ,\,\,\,{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}f(x)=-\infty .
$$

Consequently, statement I is false and II is true.

Finally, since both left and right-sided limits at $x=-2$ are different, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-2)}f(x)=\text{DNE},
$$

and therefore III is also true.

In conclusion, only statements II and III are true. A plot of the function is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14196482/assets/25e672e71c4268193c128687ba35eeca1e4bce8f0c355922a3b5df022740159c.png)

questions.problem:
Given that $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}+4x}{{x}^{2}+3x-4},$ which of the following statements is correct?

I. ${lim}_{x\to (-4)^{-}}f(x)=\infty $

II. ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x)=-\infty $

III. ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x)=-\infty $
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's factor the numerator and denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}+4x}{{x}^{2}+3x-4} \\  & =\frac{x(x+4)}{(x+4)(x-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain is  $x\ne -4,1,$ and we notice that the function can be simplified:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)=\frac{x}{x-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we see that the function has the only vertical asymptote $x=1.$ So statement I is false.

To find  ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x),$ and  ${lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x),$ we evaluate $f(x)$ at $x$-values very close to $x=1$ from the left and right.

| $x$ | $0.99$ | $0.999$ | $1$ | $1.001$ | $1.01$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $-99$ | $-999$ | $\text{undefined}$ | $1\,001$ | $101$ |

All values are negative and get smaller and smaller as $x\to 1$ from the left and all values are positive and get larger and larger as $x\to 1$ from the right. Therefore, 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x)=-\infty ,\,{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x)=\infty 
$$

Consequently, statement II is false and statement III is true.

In conclusion, only statement III is correct. A plot of the function is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14196482/assets/3de7d0a26f6f171fc83bd885eed9ff9f50bddfc76b2f58e9477241fb874c9b7d.png)
